Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

guilty adjective

of a crime

also found guilty, guilty of, convicted

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 56
Cic. Off. 2.51: nocentem aliquando, modo nē nefārium impiumque dēfendere

nocēns, nocentis

guilty, culpable

The opposite of innocēns; as a noun, a guilty person.

Examples

  • innocēns, sī accūsātus sit, absolvī potest, nocēns, nisi accūsātus fuerit, condemnārī nōn potest

    an innocent man, if he is accused, can be acquitted; a guilty one cannot be found guilty unless he has been accusedCic. Rosc. Am. 56

  • Estne absolūtus an condemnātus?

    Was he acquitted or found guilty?Traupman 191

Other words

  • sōns, sontis — guilty; as a noun, the guilty, offenders

    also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.18: comprehēnsiō sontium; Traupman 195

    As an adjective mostly in the poets; in prose chiefly the noun (Lewis & Short).

  • condemnō, condemnāre, condemnāvī, condemnātum — find guilty, convict

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 56: condemnārī nōn potest; Traupman 191, 194

    To be found guilty, condemnārī or damnārī.

See also innocent, trial, guilty, crime, criminal.

SourcesLewis & Short: noceo · Lewis & Short: sons · Lewis & Short: condemno
